cards.explanation: The answer is Jesus Himself. He says, "If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first." He puts His own name at the front of the line, friends. The disciples aren't hearing about something that skipped over Him. (John 15:18)

The answer is love. Jesus says, "If you were of the world, it would love you as its own." Then He says the world hates them instead, because they are not of the world. He has chosen them out of it, friends. (John 15:19)

The answer is that they will persecute the disciples as well. Jesus says, "If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well…" He lines it up straight, bakers, no sugar on top. He isn't springing it on them later. He's telling them up front. (John 15:20)

The answer is True! Jesus says it right after the persecution line: "if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well." He doesn't leave the disciples with only the heavy half, friends. He gives the other half too. (John 15:20)

The answer is the One who sent Him. Jesus says they will treat the disciples like this "…because of My name, since they do not know the One who sent Me." The trouble is tied to His name and to not knowing the One who sent Him, bakers. That's what He tells them. (John 15:21)

The answer is False. Jesus says, "If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin." Then He says, "Now, however, they have no excuse for their sin." He did come, and He did speak. It's a heavy line, friends. (John 15:22)
The answer is His Father! Jesus says, "Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well." It's one short line, bakers. The hatred doesn't stop at Jesus, and He says so plainly. (John 15:23)

The answer is False. Jesus says He did works among them that no one else did, and that "…now they have seen and hated both Me and My Father." They saw the works, friends. It's the hatred that's the heavy part. (John 15:24)
The answer is False. Jesus says the line written in their Law is, "They hated Me without reason." There's no good reason in it, bakers. He says this hatred fulfills what is written. (John 15:25)

The answer is that the Advocate will testify about Jesus! Jesus says the Advocate, the Spirit of truth, "…will testify about Me." The Advocate comes from the Father, and Jesus says He will send Him. That's the hope I was hollering about, friends. (John 15:26)

The answer is True. Jesus says, "And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning." Just before that, He says the Advocate will testify about Him. The disciples must testify too, bakers, and Jesus gives their time with Him as the reason. (John 15:26-27)
The answer is so they will not fall away. Jesus says, "I have told you these things so that you will not fall away." That's the purpose He gives, friends. The verse says it plainly. (John 16:1)

The answer is offering a service to God. Jesus says, "…a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God." The word that matters is think, bakers. This is a heavy line, and Jesus says it plainly. (John 16:2)

The answer is remember. Jesus says, "…I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you will remember that I told you about them." He's telling them early, friends. That way, when the hour comes, they'll remember He said it. (John 16:4)

The answer is False. Jesus says, "I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you." He's saying it now, bakers. The text gives that reason, so I don't have to guess. (John 16:4)
